newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon rebuffs Jordanian protest on freed Iraqis.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon rebuffs Jordanian protest on freed Iraqis.

text.p: Lebanon rebuffed on Saturday a Jordanian protest against its release of three Iraqi diplomats arrested in 1994 on suspicion of murdering an Iraqi dissident in Beirut, an official source said.
The dead dissident, Taleb as-Suheil, held Jordanian as well as Iraqi citizenship.

Jordan protested to Lebanon on Thursday when it freed the three men, and Lebanese Foreign Ministry Director-General Zafer al-Hassan summoned Jordanian Ambassador Fakhry Abou Taleb on Saturday to hand him a written reply, the source said.
"Hassan told Abou Taleb Lebanon insists on its commitment to international agreements and on its obligation towards diplomats on its soil," he said.
"Lebanon is complying with non-interference in other countries' affairs and expects other countries not to interfere in its internal affairs," he added.
Foreign Minister Faris Bouez said on Wednesday that under international law Lebanon could not try the three Iraqis since they had diplomatic immunity, but it could expel them.
The three diplomats, Mohammad Kazem, Ali Darwish and Hadi Hassan, who were released on 50,000 Lebanese pounds ($32) bail each, had been arrested immediately after Suheil's April 12, 1994, murder.
A fourth arrested diplomat, commercial attache Khaled Khalaf, died in custody of a brain haemorrhage in June 1995.
Beirut broke diplomatic ties with Baghdad after Suheil's murder and has not yet restored them.
